original_interpretation: SEMI's June 2023 release restated 2021 materials revenue to US$66.8bn (US$66,776m) vs US$64.3bn first reported in March 2022.
evidence_found: "surpassing the previous market high of $66.8 billion set in 2021"; table "Total | $66,776 | $72,691 | 8.9 %"; "** 2021 data reflects current updates." (PR Newswire, 13 Jun 2023). First-reported 64.3 confirmed in SRC-0599.
notes: PR Newswire is SEMI's own distribution of the release, so industry_body is fair.

original_interpretation: SEMI first reported 2021 global materials revenue as US$64.3bn.
evidence_found: "The global semiconductor materials market grew 15.9% to $64.3 billion in revenue in 2021, surpassing the previous market high of $55.5 billion set in 2020" (PR Newswire, 16 Mar 2022, para 1); table total $64,273.
notes: Later restated to US$66.8bn (CLM-1798); the claim already flags 'as first reported'. Estimate type is right (SEMI MMDS compilation).

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated 2021 wafer fab materials revenue at US$40.4bn.
evidence_found: "Wafer fabrication materials and packaging materials revenues in 2021 totaled $40.4 billion and $23.9 billion, respectively, for year-over-year increases of 15.5% and 16.5%." (para 2)
notes: As first reported (March 2022); 2021 total later restated upward.

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated 2021 packaging materials revenue at US$23.9bn.
evidence_found: "Wafer fabrication materials and packaging materials revenues in 2021 totaled $40.4 billion and $23.9 billion, respectively" (para 2)
notes: As first reported (March 2022).

original_interpretation: SEMI's March 2022 release restated 2020 to US$55.5bn (US$55,479m) vs US$55.3bn first reported March 2021.
evidence_found: "surpassing the previous market high of $55.5 billion set in 2020"; "Total | $55,479 | $64,273 | 15.9%"; "** 2020 data reflect current updates." (SRC-0599). March 2021 release: "grew 4.9% in 2020 to $55.3 billion" (SRC-0600).

original_interpretation: SEMI first reported 2020 materials revenue as US$55.3bn.
evidence_found: "The global semiconductor materials market grew 4.9% in 2020 to $55.3 billion in revenue, surpassing the previous market high of $52.9 billion set in 2018" (SEMI, 22 Mar 2021, para 1)

original_interpretation: SEMI's March 2021 release put 2019 materials revenue at US$52.7bn (table US$52,716m).
evidence_found: Table '2019 and 2020 Regional Semiconductor Materials Markets (US$ Billions)': "Total | $52,716 | $55,308 | 4.9%"; "** 2019 data have been updated based on SEMI's data collection programs."
notes: Table header says 'US$ Billions' but values are clearly US$ millions (total 55,308 = $55.3bn). 2019 (52.7) is below the 2018 high of 52.9 cited in the same release, consistent with a 2019 decline.

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated 2020 wafer fab materials revenue at US$34.9bn.
evidence_found: "Wafer fabrication materials and packaging materials revenues totaled $34.9 billion and $20.4 billion, respectively, in 2020 for year-over-year increases of 6.5% and 2.3%." (para 2)
notes: As first reported (March 2021).

original_interpretation: SEMI estimated 2020 packaging materials revenue at US$20.4bn.
evidence_found: "Wafer fabrication materials and packaging materials revenues totaled $34.9 billion and $20.4 billion, respectively, in 2020" (para 2)
notes: As first reported (March 2021).

original_interpretation: China overtook South Korea as no. 2 materials consumer in 2020 (SEMI).
evidence_found: "With its aggressive capacity build-up, China surpassed Korea to claim the second spot." (para 3); table 2020: China $9,763 vs South Korea $9,231; 2019: China $8,717 vs Korea $8,885.
notes: Ranking rests on SEMI's modelled ship-to estimates, so 'estimate' would be a more precise claim_type than 'fact'; attribution to SEMI keeps it honest.

original_interpretation: 2019 materials consumption: Taiwan US$11,449m, China US$8,717m, South Korea US$8,885m (SEMI, March 2021).
notes: Values are US$ millions despite the table header 'US$ Billions'.

original_interpretation: SEMI classifies wafer-patterning materials as Fab Materials: silicon, SOI, photomasks, photoresist, ancillaries, gases, chemicals, targets, CMP.
evidence_found: "Materials used to pattern the wafer are classified as \"Fab Materials\", while those used to protect and/or connect the die are referred to as \"Packing Materials\"." Table: "Fab Materials - Silicon - SOI - Photomasks - Photoresist - Photoresist Ancillaries - Gases - Chemicals - Targets - CMP" (Coverage taxonomy, www.semi.org)
notes: SRC-0601 (prod8.semi.org) returned a Cloudflare bot check in both web_extract and the browser; verified against the identical page on www.semi.org (/en/ and /sea/ paths both show the same lists).

original_interpretation: SEMI packaging categories: leadframes, substrates, bonding wire, die attach, mold compounds, encapsulants, ceramic packages, other.
evidence_found: "Packaging Materials - Leadframes - Substrates - Bonding Wire - Die Attach - Mold Compounds - Encapsulants - Ceramic Packages - Other Packaging Materials" (Coverage taxonomy table, www.semi.org)
notes: SRC-0601 host blocked by Cloudflare; checked on the same page at www.semi.org.

original_interpretation: MMDS one-sheet: 10 wafer-fab and 6 packaging segments, by category and ship-to region.
evidence_found: "Historical annual revenue of semiconductor materials by category and “ship-to” market region and forecast through next year." "Contains 10 segments for wafer fab related materials and 6 segments for packaging related materials." (Report highlights, MMDS one-sheet 2025)
notes: Counts differ from the 9/8 public taxonomy (CON-0061 stands).

original_interpretation: SEMI EMG represents suppliers of substrates, polymers, metals, chemicals, gases; chapters in America, Korea, Japan, Europe plus SEMI Taiwan Materials Committee; SMG sits within it.
evidence_found: "The Electronic Materials Group (EMG) is a technology community representing SEMI member companies that provide substrates, polymers, metals, organic and inorganic materials, chemicals, and gases" ... "A subset of EMG, the Silicon Manufacturers Group (SMG) is a sub-group under the EMG unbrella." ... "four chapters located in America, Korea, Japan, and Europe. There is also a SEMI Taiwan Materials Committee."
notes: URL now resolves to /en/communities/emg. Page also says the Compound Semiconductor Group operates within EMG. Self-description of an association; acceptable as fact about its own structure.

original_interpretation: EC: nearly 500 specialised process chemicals; names Shin-Etsu, Sumitomo, Mitsui, BASF, Linde, Merck, Air Liquide, TSCC, Dow/DuPont.
evidence_found: "Chip manufacturing requires nearly 500 specialised process chemicals; this number is rising as semiconductors become more complex. Key suppliers are Shin-Etsu Chemicals, Sumitomo Chemicals, Mitsui Chemicals (Japan), BASF, Linde, Merck KGaA, Air Liquide (EU), Taiwan Specialty Chemicals Corporation, and in Dow/DuPont (US)." (SWD(2022) 147, p. 8)

original_interpretation: EC ranks Shin-Etsu then SUMCO largest wafer makers, followed by GlobalWafers, Siltronic, SK Siltron, Soitec.
evidence_found: "Japan's Shin-Etsu and Sumco are the world's largest silicon wafer makers respectively, followed by Taiwan’s GlobalWafers, Germany’s Siltronic, Korea's SK Siltron and France's Soitec." (p. 8)
notes: Ordering only; no shares, basis or year given (circa 2021-22).

original_interpretation: In Feb 2019 a faulty photoresist batch forced TSMC to scrap wafers worth about US$550m (EC citing press).
evidence_found: EC p. 12: "in February 2019, a faulty batch of photoresist chemicals forced TSMC to scrap a large quantity of silicon wafers with a value of USD 550 million". TSMC primary (15 Feb 2019): "This incident is expected to reduce Q1 revenue by about US$550 million" and "The wafers scrapped in Q1 will be made up in Q2. This will contribute about US$550 million to Q2 revenue".
correction: The EC does say this, but per TSMC's own release US$550m was the expected Q1 2019 revenue reduction (guidance), largely recovered in Q2, not a measured value of scrapped wafers; the incident (Jan 2019 detection, 12/16 nm at Fab 14B) was announced in February. See superseding claim.
notes: Secondary rendering of a company guidance figure; superseding claim added from the TSMC primary document.

original_interpretation: EC: closure of 3M's Belgian fluorinated-coolant plant raised concern as there is no alternative supplier.
evidence_found: "the closure of the 3M plant in Belgium, which produces fluorinated coolant for semiconductor manufacturing, has led to major concerns in the industry as there is no alternative supplier20" (p. 12)
notes: EC relies on a press footnote (fn 20); 'no alternative supplier' is the EC's characterisation as of 2022, not an established market fact.

original_interpretation: EC: ABF substrates from Japan and Taiwan essential for laminated packaging; shortages caused delays and price rises.
evidence_found: "Ajinomoto Build-up Film (ABF) substrates produced in Japan and Taiwan are essential for every chip that uses laminated packaging. ... Shortages have persisted for some time22 and are causing delays in chip production as well as price increases." (p. 12)
notes: Describes the 2021-22 shortage period.

original_interpretation: ITA: Shin-Etsu and SUMCO hold about 90% of the global silicon wafer market.
evidence_found: "Shin-Etsu Chemical and SUMCO dominate the global silicon wafer market segment with approximately 90% of the market." (Semiconductor Materials section, ITA Japan Semiconductors guide)
notes: Attribution verified; the figure itself is unsourced and conflicts with Brookings' 53% for Japan and with the EC's list of four large non-Japanese wafer makers (CON-0057). Page has no visible publication date; it references SEMICON Japan Dec 2025 and a 2025-11 image path, so it is a late-2025 edition.

original_interpretation: ITA: Japanese firms such as JSR and TOK hold about 90% of photoresist market.
evidence_found: "In the photoresist field, several Japanese firms such as JSR and Tokyo Ohka Kogyo hold about 90% of the global market."
notes: Attribution verified; no basis or year given; see CON-0058 (Brookings: 50%).

original_interpretation: ITA: Japanese companies about 30% of photomask market.
evidence_found: "Japanese companies account for approximately 30% of the global photomask market."
notes: No basis stated (merchant vs captive photomasks unclear).

original_interpretation: ITA citing Brookings (June 2024): Japan 53% of silicon wafers, 50% of photoresists.
evidence_found: ITA: "As reported by the Brookings Institute in June 2024, Japan has almost 88% global market share for semiconductor coater/developers, 53% global market share for silicon wafers, and 50% global market share for photoresists." Brookings original (3 Jun 2024): "Japan holds an 88% global market share for coater/developers (Tokyo Electron, Screen Holdings), 53% for silicon wafers (Shin-Etsu Chemical, Sumco), and 50% for photoresists (Shin-Etsu, JSR, Tokyo Ohka Kogyo)."
notes: Brookings original opened (CON-0057 said it was not); figures match. Brookings is a Q&A commentary (Mathieu Duchâtel) whose figures link to a Nikkei Asia article, so the numbers are still third-hand with no stated basis or year.

original_interpretation: METI May 2024: subsidised SUMCO 300 mm expansion in Imari/Yoshinogari, crystal 200k/month-eq and wafers 100k/month from Oct 2029; ¥225bn project, ¥75bn max subsidy.
evidence_found: SRC-0606 p. 11 row: "SUMCO シリコンウエハ 佐賀県伊万里市 佐賀県吉野ヶ里町 結晶：2029年10月 ウエハ：2029年10月 結晶:20万枚/月相当 ウエハ:10万枚/月 2,250 750". METI amended certification (27 Mar 2026): sites "佐賀県伊万里市、山形県米沢市"; "必要な資金の額：580 億円（最大助成額：193 億円）".
correction: Accurate for the May 2024 list, but METI amended the certification on 2026-03-27: the plan now upgrades existing lines at Imari (Kuhara, Nagahama) and Yonezawa, required funds ¥58bn, maximum subsidy ¥19.3bn, supply from Jan 2028 to Mar 2031; the Yoshinogari plant was postponed. See superseding claims.
notes: The May 2024 table row does not itself say 300 mm (that appears in the Kyushu map, p. 9, and the 2026 certification). REL-0287 (METI subsidizes SUMCO, up to ¥75bn) should be re-pointed to the superseding claim.

original_interpretation: METI May 2024: subsidised FC-BGA expansions by Ibiden (Gifu, +12% from Sep 2025) and Shinko (Nagano, +6% from Jul 2029).
evidence_found: Rows under 部素材: "イビデン FC‐BGA基板 岐阜県大野町 2025年9月 現状比約12%増強 ー 405"; "新光電気工業 FC‐BGA基板 長野県千曲市 2029年7月 現状比約6%増強 533 178" (SRC-0606, p. 11; last two columns 事業総額 / 最大助成額, 億円)
notes: Max subsidies: Ibiden ¥40.5bn (project total not shown), Shinko ¥17.8bn of ¥53.3bn. Status of these schedules after May 2024 not checked.

original_interpretation: METI fund supports neon recycling (Sony, Kioxia), helium stockpiling (Iwatani, Air Water) and rare-gas production (Taiyo Nippon Sanso neon 27m L/yr from Apr 2026; Nippon Air Liquide).
evidence_found: Rows under 原料: "ソニーセミコン ネオン（リサイクル）"; "キオクシア ネオン（リサイクル）"; "岩谷産業、岩谷瓦斯 ヘリウム（備蓄）"; "大陽日酸 希ガス（生産） 千葉県君津市等 2026年4月 ネオン：2,700万ℓ/年"; "日本エア・リキード 希ガス（生産）"; "エア・ウォーター 日本ヘリウム ヘリウム（備蓄）" (SRC-0606, p. 11)
notes: 2,700万ℓ = 27 million litres; also krypton 2m L/yr and xenon 0.25m L/yr. The list also includes JFE Steel/Tokyo Gas Chemical (rare gases), Koatsu Gas Kogyo (helium recycling), Sumitomo Corp (yellow phosphorus) and Rasa Industries (phosphoric acid), not mentioned in the claim.

original_interpretation: METI economic-security fund (FY2022 supplementary ¥368.6bn) approved 18 projects worth about ¥336.9bn as of 8 Dec 2023.
evidence_found: "経済安保基金による半導体サプライチェーン強靭化支援 【R4補正:3,686億円】 ＜採択案件一覧（※2023年12月8日時点）＞ 合計1８件、約3,369億円" (SRC-0606, p. 11)
correction: Clarification: the ¥336.9bn is the sum of the 最大助成額 (maximum subsidy) column, not total project cost. My sum of that column across the 18 rows = 3,369.2 oku yen; the 事業総額 column sums to far more (over ¥810bn where shown).
notes: Resolves the ambiguity flagged in the claim's notes; metric unit (JPY 100m) correct.
